commons-nesting-check.desc: Verifies that `t` and `s` commons modules (see import-rules check) are not nested (i.e. a `t` module having a `t` ancestor (e.g. `t/t`, `t/foo/t`, or `t/foo/t.rs`) is a violation, and likewise for `s`).
commons-nesting-check.rationale: A simplification because it seems nesting these wouldn't be very common or useful
